title: Informal emails and messages
subtitle: be in touch, fancy, get together, all the best
summary: Write a friendly email or message with the phrases English speakers really use to friends and family.

lesson.heading: A model email to a friend
lesson.text: Read this short thank-you email and learn the phrases in bold. Informal emails start with **Hi**, **Hello** or **Dear** + first name.

examples.text: **Just a quick message to** thank you for dinner last night.
I really enjoyed meeting your friend Alice. She's **a laugh**, isn't she?
I'm **hoping to** get tickets for the film festival next week.
I'll **be in touch** to see if there's anything you **fancy** seeing.
examples.note: be in touch = make contact; fancy = want (to see)

examples.text: **Give my regards to** Conrad, and **once again**, thanks for last night.
examples.note: give my regards to = say hello to ... from me; once again = again, as before

lesson.heading: How to begin and end an informal email
rows: a close friend or family member
lesson.note: With family and very close friends we say **give my love to**; with other people, **give my regards to**.

lesson.heading: A model message conversation
lesson.text: Short messages use the same phrases. **It's ages since ...** means a long time has passed; **in two weeks' time** means two weeks from now.

examples.text: Sorry it's been **ages since** I last got in touch.
examples.note: ages = a long time; since = from a time in the past until now

examples.text: I just wanted to **let you know** that I'm coming to Birmingham.
I'm coming **in two weeks' time** - **actually** just before your birthday.
Could we **get together** and go out for a meal?
examples.note: get together = meet for a social reason

examples.text: Maybe Mark could **join us** as well?
**Anyway**, better get back to work. See you soon!
examples.note: anyway = used to change the subject or end a conversation

lesson.heading: actually
lesson.text: **Actually** gives more exact information, or says something surprising. It means the same as **in fact**. It does *not* mean *at the moment*.

examples.text: He looks Italian, but **actually** he's not.
It looks new, but **in fact** it isn't.

examples.wrong: The land is actually for sale

lesson.heading: Useful informal phrases
rows: make contact by phone, email or text
a long time has passed since ...

lesson.text: Note the apostrophe in in two weeks' time and in a week's time - the time word is possessive.

exercises.prompt: Match each phrase with its meaning.
Which ending is right for an email to your sister?
exercises.explanation: Love or Lots of love is for a close friend or family member.

exercises.prompt: Which ending is right for an email to a friend you do not know very well?
exercises.explanation: Best wishes and All the best are friendly but not too close.

exercises.prompt: Rewrite with FANCY: 'Do you want to go?' -> 'Do you ___ going?'
Rewrite with TOUCH: 'I'll write soon.' -> 'I'll ___ soon.'
exercises.explanation: Be in touch / get in touch = make contact.

exercises.prompt: Rewrite with FACT: 'It looks new, but actually it isn't.' -> 'It looks new, but ___ it isn't.'
exercises.explanation: In fact means the same as actually.

exercises.prompt: Rewrite with LET: 'I'll tell you as soon as possible.' -> 'I'll ___ as soon as possible.'
Rewrite with IN: 'I'm going three weeks from now.' -> 'I'm going ___.'
exercises.explanation: In three weeks' time = three weeks from now.

exercises.prompt: Rewrite with LAUGH: 'Jamie is very funny.' -> 'Jamie is ___.'
Rewrite with SINCE: 'I haven't written for ages.' -> 'It's ___ I wrote.'
exercises.explanation: It's ages since I wrote = a long time has passed.

exercises.prompt: Email: 'I've been really busy ___ I last wrote.'
exercises.explanation: Since = from a time in the past until now.

exercises.prompt: Email: 'It would be great if we could get ___, and maybe Filipe could join us.'
exercises.explanation: Get together = meet for a social reason.

exercises.prompt: Email: '___, I'll write again soon. I hope things are going well with you.'
exercises.explanation: Anyway changes the subject or closes a message.

exercises.statement: 'The house is actually for sale' means the house is for sale at the moment.
exercises.explanation: Actually means in fact, not at the moment. Say: The house is currently for sale.
